P1: Timing-unsafe signature comparison. Using `===` to compare HMAC signatures leaks timing information, enabling an attacker to forge valid signatures incrementally. Use a constant-time comparison instead.

A portable approach (no Node.js `timingSafeEqual` dependency) is to XOR the byte representations:</violation>

<file name="packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/namespace.py">

<violation number="1" location="packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/namespace.py:34">
P1: `parse_table_name` cannot correctly round-trip names produced by `get_table_name` for the default namespace. When `get_table_name` returns just the bare model name (no prefix for the default namespace), `parse_table_name` will incorrectly split on any separator character found *within* the model name itself.

For example with the default `"_"` separator: `get_table_name("user_posts")` → `"user_posts"`, then `parse_table_name("user_posts")` → `("user", "posts")` instead of `("default", "user_posts")`.

Consider keeping a registry of known namespaces, or always including the namespace prefix (even for the default) so parsing is unambiguous.</violation>
</file>
